classification.difficultyReason: Apply the perpendicular radius-tangent theorem at both ends of a diameter and infer parallel lines.

content.prompt: Prove that the tangents at the endpoints of a diameter are parallel. Let PAQ and UBV be the tangents at the endpoints of a diameter AOB. Prove that $PQ\parallel UV$.

spec.description: Diameter AOB and tangents PAQ/UBV at A/B. No added parallel arrows or perpendicular symbols.
spec.answerVisibility: Original supplied givens and targets only; no derived numerical values or proof conclusions.

answer.short: $PQ\parallel UV$: both tangents are perpendicular to diameter AB.
answer.worked: A radius is perpendicular to the tangent at its endpoint, so $PQ\perp AB$ at A and $UV\perp AB$ at B. Lines perpendicular to the same line are parallel; hence $PQ\parallel UV$.
